Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Town, shops & places

urban adjective

also of the city, city (as in city life), town (as in town life)

classical

Varr. RR 3.1.1: rūstica et urbāna vīta (Lewis & Short)

urbānus, urbāna, urbānum

Declension on Wiktionary

of the city, urban

Of the city, as against rūsticus; at Rome, of Rome itself. Very often it means refined, polished, and witty: urbānitās is good manners and wit (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • oppidānus, oppidāna, oppidānum — of a town; provincial

    also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.240: senex quīdam oppidānus (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of a country town rather than the capital, and so sometimes provincial, small-town; as a noun, oppidānī are the townspeople (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • annum ita dīvīsērunt, ut nōnīs modo diēbus urbānās rēs ūsurpārent, reliquīs septem ut rūra colerent

    they divided the year so that they attended to town business only on every ninth day, and farmed the land on the other sevenVarr. RR 2 praef. 1

  • duae vītae hominum, rūstica et urbāna

    the two ways men live, in the country and in the townCic. Rosc. Am. 48 (Lewis & Short)

See also rural, city, town.
